items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1972-06-26
items.q: I was learning music when I was a Tio. I took lessons two years without the instrument.

ctx.x: What did they teach you? You reminded me of something. What about vibrato when you were studying under Tio?

Well, I had to study that. That's a different study. I was learning music when I was a Tio. I took lessons two years without the instrument. I was small. I was about nine years old. Then when I got to be eleven, they gave me the clarinet. Well, I knew the clarinet. My uncle was junior, you know.
I used to watch him all the time.

items.title: Albert Nicholas Interview, 1967-02-09
items.q: Then Lorenzo Teo, his son. And finished up with him until around 1915.

ctx.x: Can you tell us something about your training and taking lessons and so on?

Well, I started taking lessons around 9 years of age with my uncle, Wooden Joe Nicholas. He was my big influence on this jazz scene. And later on, I went to Papa Teo and took lessons with him for about a couple of years. Then Lorenzo Teo, his son. And finished up with him until around 1915. Then I started to go pro. My first gigs around New Orleans was with the Maple Leaf Band. Then Buddy Petite's Band. When Jimmy Noon left to go to Chicago, I played with Buddy Petite and several other bands around New Orleans.…
